title: 第九十八章剑指苍穹第九十七章江山如画
content_zh:
推荐各位书友阅读：长安剑客萧书生贰正文第九十八章剑指苍穹（..la）大乾天启十七年，秋。
长安的雨，绵密如针，缠缠绵绵落了三日。
烟雨笼住整座帝都，朱墙金瓦褪去了往日的煌煌盛气，被一层朦胧水雾裹着，多了几分沉郁的压抑。朱雀大街青石地面被雨水冲刷得油亮，倒映着两侧连绵的楼阁飞檐，也倒映着往来行人步履匆匆的剪影。昔日车水马龙、人声鼎沸的帝都主干道，此刻竟透着一种死寂的肃穆，连街边常年喧嚣的酒肆茶楼，都敛了声响，门窗半掩，隐隐透出窥伺的目光。
今日的长安，无人敢高声言语。
只因三日前，镇北侯府满门被拘的诏令，传遍了九城十二坊。
而此刻，皇城承天门外，雨幕之中，一道孤峭的身影，静静立在积水的长街之上。
萧琰身着一袭洗得发白的玄色劲装，衣摆边角带着细微的磨损，那是常年征战边关、浴血厮杀留下的痕迹。他身姿挺拔如松，脊背挺直，未曾有半分弯折，即便身陷绝境，依旧守着一身傲骨。少年不过十九岁年纪，面容清俊凌厉，眉眼间尚未褪去少年人的清朗，却早已沉淀了远超同龄人的沧桑与冷冽。眉骨锋利，眼眸漆黑如深潭，不见半分波澜，唯有眼底深处，藏着一丝未灭的星火，滚烫而倔强。
他腰间悬着一柄古朴长剑，剑身无华，剑鞘是经年的黑檀木，刻着细密的云纹，早已被岁月摩挲得温润发亮。此剑名“破穹”，是他十五岁入北境、斩杀第一尊蛮族大祭司后，亲手锻造的佩剑，四年光阴，随他踏遍北境万里疆土，斩敌无数，饮尽胡尘血水，陪他从无名少年，打成震慑北疆的少年战神。
只是今日，这柄斩尽蛮夷、护佑大夏山河的利剑，却被一纸莫须有的罪名，囚于帝都，蒙尘受辱。
承天门高耸巍峨，朱红大门紧闭，鎏金铜钉在烟雨里黯淡无光，如同帝王冰冷的眉眼，隔绝了殿内的荣华权柄，也隔绝了殿外少年的赤诚忠心。宫门两侧，铁甲禁军肃立如山，银甲沐雨，长枪垂地，森寒的枪尖对准雨中的少年，每一道目光都带着戒备与疏离。他们曾无数次听闻这位少年战神的威名，曾敬佩他镇守北境、护国安民的功绩，可君命如山，他们只能恪守职责，将利刃对准昔日的护国功臣。
无人言语，唯有雨声淅沥，敲打着宫阙琉璃，敲打着青石长街，也敲打着萧琰冰冷的心房。
三日前，一道密诏自皇城而出，直指镇北侯府通敌叛国、私蓄兵权、暗通北境蛮族。一纸轻飘飘的诏书，撕碎了萧家四代忠良、镇守北疆百年的赫赫荣光。
镇北侯萧振远，也就是萧琰的生父，半生戎马，镇守北境四十载，击退蛮族七十二次入侵，收复失地千里，护得大夏北疆百姓安居乐业、百年无大战。最终却落得个打入天牢、等候秋后问斩的结局。萧府上下百余口人，尽数被拘，仆从幕僚无一幸免，昔日门庭显赫、车马盈门的镇北侯府，一夜之间沦为罪府，高墙锁尽凄凉。
唯有萧琰，因半月前孤身自北境千里奔袭、回京述职，恰逢朝堂剧变，又因他手握北境三十万边军军心，帝王忌惮、权臣构陷，未曾即刻定罪，只被勒令禁足长安，不得离城半步，等候三司会审。
说是候审，实则已是待罪之身。
世人皆知，所谓三司会审，不过是帝王为安抚北境军心、掩人耳目的幌子。朝野上下，文武百官，无人敢为萧家发声，无人敢替这位少年战神辩驳半句。昔日那些受过萧家恩惠、与侯府交好的权贵朝臣，尽数闭门避祸，唯恐沾染半分牵连，纷纷与萧府划清界限，极尽冷漠势利。
繁华帝都，万丈红尘，一朝落难，尽是凉薄。
雨丝落在萧琰的发间、肩头，冰凉刺骨，顺着发丝滑落，浸透衣衫，可他身形未动分毫，宛若一尊屹立风雨中的青石雕像。自清晨立于承天门外，他已足足伫立三个时辰，不言不语，不卑不亢，既不求饶，亦不辩解。
他在等，等最后一丝念想落幕，等最后一丝赤诚散尽。
“萧琰。”

良久，厚重的宫门之内，终于传来一道苍老沉缓的声音，穿透淅沥雨声，清晰落在耳畔。
宫门缓缓开启一道缝隙，一名身着紫袍、腰佩玉牌的内侍缓步走出，雨水打湿了他的袍角，他却步履端庄，眉眼间带着皇家内侍特有的疏离与肃穆。此人是宫中总管太监李全安，侍奉帝王数十年，深得圣宠，今日奉命传旨，便是朝堂对萧琰最后的处置。
李全安走到萧琰身前三步之遥站定，目光扫过少年淋透的身影，看着他眼底毫无波澜的沉静，心中暗自叹息，面上却依旧不苟言笑，展开手中明黄圣旨，朗声宣读。
“奉天承运皇帝，诏曰：镇北侯萧振远私通敌寇，罪证确凿，累及宗族。其子萧琰，虽年少有功，然失察纵容，难辞其咎。念其北境四年，屡立战功，斩杀敌酋，戍守边疆，略有微功，特免其死罪，削去镇北世子爵位，剥夺北境兵权，贬为白身，逐出长安，永世不得返京。钦此。”
字字铿锵，句句冰冷。
没有半分查证，没有半分体恤，一纸诏书，轻飘飘抹去萧家四代忠名，抹去萧琰四年浴血拼杀的所有功绩。四年北境风霜，枕戈待旦，浴血沙场，多少次九死一生，多少次孤身御敌，换来的，便是一句失察纵容，一纸逐出帝都、永世不得归京的贬令。
雨声更急，风声呼啸，卷着寒意掠过长街。
李全安收起圣旨，看着眼前沉默不语的少年，语气稍缓，带着一丝不易察觉的惋惜：“萧公子，接旨吧。陛下仁慈，留你性命，已是天大的恩典。离开长安，自此凡尘两断，尚可保全自身。”
恩典？
萧琰缓缓抬眼，漆黑的眸子望向巍峨的皇城宫阙，望向那层层叠叠的朱墙金瓦。那里是大夏权力的巅峰，是他世代效忠的君王居所，是他少年时满心向往、誓死守护的家国朝堂。可如今，这座金碧辉煌的城池，却亲手碾碎了他的忠诚，辜负了他的热血，葬送了他满门忠良。
他嘴角微微勾起一抹极淡的弧度，似自嘲，似冷笑，无声无息，却藏着彻骨的寒凉。
“我萧家四代戍边，百年忠骨，护大夏北疆安稳，护帝都万民安乐。”
萧琰的声音低沉沙哑，被风雨打磨得清冷凛冽，不高，却字字清晰，穿透漫天雨幕，震得在场禁军皆是心头一颤。
“我父镇守北疆四十载，身经百战，伤痕累累，从未有半分叛心。我萧琰十九岁，四年北境，斩蛮族大将一十三人，破敌阵二十七座，守得边疆万里无寇，护得边境百姓无虞。”
“何谓通敌？何谓失察？”
他声声质问，没有暴怒咆哮，只有一片死寂的冰冷，却比嘶吼更具力量，压得周遭风雨都似凝滞片刻。
content_en:
Recommended reading for all book friends: Chapter 98 of Chang'an Swordsman Xiao Shusheng II (The Sword Points to the Sky (..la)) Autumn, the seventeenth year of the Daqian Apocalypse.
The rain in Chang'an was as dense as needles and lingered for three days.
Mist and rain enveloped the entire imperial capital. The red walls and golden tiles had lost their former splendor and were enveloped in a layer of hazy mist, adding a bit of gloom and depression. The bluestone floor of Zhuque Street was washed shiny by the rain, reflecting the continuous eaves of the pavilions on both sides, as well as the hurried silhouettes of pedestrians passing by. The main road in the imperial capital that used to be bustling with traffic and people now seemed to be filled with a dead silence and solemnity. Even the noisy restaurants and restaurants on the street had muted their noises. The doors and windows were half-closed, and there was a faint peek of prying eyes.
In Chang'an today, no one dares to speak loudly.
Just because three days ago, the edict that all the people in the Zhenbei Hou Mansion were detained spread throughout the nine cities and twelve squares.
At this moment, outside the Chengtian Gate of the Imperial City, amid the rain, a lone figure stood quietly on the waterlogged long street.
Xiao Yan was dressed in black clothes that had been washed white, with slight wear and tear on the corners of the clothes, which were traces of years of fighting at the border and bloody battles. His posture is as straight as a pine tree, his back is straight and not bent at all. Even if he is in a desperate situation, he still maintains his pride. The boy was only nineteen years old, and his face was handsome and sharp. The youthful clarity had not yet faded from his brows and eyes, but he had already accumulated vicissitudes and coldness far beyond those of his peers. The brow bones are sharp, and the eyes are as dark as deep pools, with no waves at all. Only a trace of unquenched sparks are hidden deep in the eyes, hot and stubborn.
There was a simple long sword hanging on his waist. The blade was plain and the scabbard was made of aged ebony wood, engraved with fine cloud patterns. It had been rubbed by the years until it was warm and shiny. The name of this sword is "Broken Qiong". It was a sword he forged with his own hands after he entered the Northern Territory at the age of fifteen and killed the first barbarian high priest. In four years, he followed him across thousands of miles of the Northern Territory, killing countless enemies, drinking Hu Chen's blood, and accompanying him from an unknown boy to a young war god who shocked the Northern Territory.
But today, this sharp sword that cut down the barbarians and protected the mountains and rivers of Daxia was imprisoned in the imperial capital on an unfounded charge and was humiliated.
The Chengtian Gate is towering and majestic, the vermilion gate is tightly closed, and the gilt copper nails are dim in the mist and rain, like the cold eyebrows of the emperor, cutting off the glory and power in the palace, and also cutting off the sincere loyalty of the young people outside the palace. On both sides of the palace gate, the armored Imperial Guards stood as solemn as mountains, their silver armor bathed in the rain, their long spears hanging on the ground, their cold spear points pointed at the young man in the rain, with every look in their eyes filled with caution and alienation. They had heard of the reputation of this young war god countless times, and had admired his achievements in guarding the northern border and protecting the country and the people. However, the king's orders were as strong as a mountain, so they could only abide by their duties and point their sharp blades at the former heroes who protected the country.
No one spoke, only the patter of rain, beating on the palace glass, the long bluestone street, and Xiao Yan's cold heart.
Three days ago, a secret edict came out from the imperial city, pointing directly at the Zhenbei Hou Mansion for colluding with the enemy and treason, secretly amassing military power, and secretly liaising with the barbarians in the north. A fluttering edict tore into pieces the glorious glory of four generations of the Xiao family who had been loyal and guarded Northern Xinjiang for hundreds of years.
Xiao Zhenyuan, the Marquis of Zhenbei, Xiao Yan's biological father, spent his whole life as a soldier and guarded the northern border for forty years. He repelled seventy-two barbarian invasions, recovered thousands of miles of lost territory, and protected the people of Northern Xia from wars for a hundred years. In the end, he ended up being imprisoned in the sky and waiting to be executed by his queen. More than a hundred people in the Xiao Mansion were all detained, and none of the servants and staff were spared. The Zhenbei Hou Mansion, which used to have a prominent courtyard and full of carriages and horses, turned into a crime house overnight, with high walls and a desolate atmosphere.
Only Xiao Yan, because he had traveled thousands of miles from the north to report his duties alone half a month ago, coincided with the dramatic changes in the court, and because he had the hearts and minds of the 300,000 border troops in the north, the emperor was afraid, and the powerful officials were trying to frame him, so he was not immediately convicted. He was only ordered to be banned from Chang'an, and was not allowed to leave the city even half a step, pending the trial of the three divisions.
He is said to be awaiting trial, but in fact he is already awaiting trial.
As everyone knows, the so-called Three Divisions MeetingThe trial was just a cover for the emperor to appease the troops in the north and cover up the public. No one dared to speak out for the Xiao family, no one dared to defend the young God of War. In the past, all the powerful courtiers who had received favors from the Xiao family and had good relations with the Hou Mansion closed their doors to avoid trouble. For fear of being implicated in the slightest, they drew a clear line with the Xiao Mansion, showing extreme indifference and snobbishness.
The prosperous imperial capital, thousands of miles away from the world of mortals, turned into a deserted place once it was in trouble.
Raindrops fell on Xiao Yan's hair and shoulders. It was bitingly cold, sliding down his hair and soaking through his clothes, but his figure did not move at all, like a bluestone statue standing in the wind and rain. Since he stood outside Chengtian Gate in the early morning, he has stood there for three full hours, silent, neither humble nor arrogant, neither begging for mercy nor making excuses.
He is waiting, waiting for the last trace of thought to end, waiting for the last trace of sincerity to dissipate.
"Xiao Yan."
After a long time, an old and slow voice finally came from within the thick palace door, breaking through the patter of rain and falling clearly on my ears.
The palace door slowly opened a gap, and a chamberlain wearing a purple robe and a jade medallion on his waist walked out slowly. The rainwater wet the corners of his robe, but he walked dignifiedly, with the alienation and solemnity unique to a royal chamberlain in his eyebrows. This person is Li Quan'an, the eunuch in charge of the palace. He has served the emperor for decades and has won the favor of the emperor. Today, he was ordered to deliver the edict, which was the final treatment of Xiao Yan by the court.
Li Quan'an walked to and stood three steps in front of Xiao Yan. He glanced at the young man's soaked figure and looked at the calmness in his eyes. He sighed secretly in his heart, but still had a serious smile on his face. He unfolded the bright yellow imperial edict in his hand and read it aloud.
"The emperor is destined to carry the emperor, and the edict says: Xiao Zhenyuan, the Marquis of Zhenbei, has secretly collaborated with the enemy. The evidence of the crime is conclusive and affects the clan. His son Xiao Yan, although he was young and meritorious, was negligent and indulged, and it is hard to escape the blame. For four years in the north, he has repeatedly For those who have made military exploits, killed enemy chiefs, and guarded the frontier, they will be exempted from the death penalty, deprived of the title of Viscount of Zhenbei, deprived of military power in the north, demoted to a white body, expelled from Chang'an, and never allowed to return to the capital."
Every word is sonorous and every sentence is cold.
Without any verification, without any sympathy, a piece of edict wiped away the loyal names of four generations of the Xiao family, and erased all the achievements of Xiao Yan's four-year bloody battle. Four years of hard work in the north, waiting for danger, bloody battlefields, many narrow escapes, and many times fighting against the enemy alone, all in exchange was a word of negligence and indulgence, a derogatory order to be expelled from the imperial capital, and never to return to the capital.
The sound of rain became more rapid, and the wind howled, carrying a chill across the long street.
Li Quan'an put away the imperial edict, looked at the silent young man in front of him, and said in a slightly slower tone with a hint of unnoticeable regret: "Master Xiao, accept the edict. His majesty is merciful and spares your life. It is a great grace. After leaving Chang'an, the world will be cut off from now on, so you can still save yourself."
Grace?
Xiao Yan slowly raised his eyes, his dark eyes looking at the majestic Imperial City Palace and the layers of red walls and golden tiles. It was the pinnacle of Daxia's power, the residence of the king he had loyally loyal to for generations, and the palace of his family and country that he had longed for when he was a boy and vowed to protect it to the death. But now, this splendid city has crushed his loyalty with his own hands, failed his blood, and ruined all his loyal family members.
The corner of his mouth curved slightly, as if he was mocking himself or sneering. It was silent, but it hid a bone-chilling chill.
"I, the Xiao family, have guarded the border for four generations and have been loyal for hundreds of years. I protect the stability of the northern border of Daxia and the peace and happiness of all the people in the imperial capital."
Xiao Yan's voice was low and hoarse, polished by the wind and rain, cold and cold. It was not high, but the words were clear, penetrating through the rainy sky, and making all the guards present tremble.
"My father has been guarding the northern border for forty years. He has gone through hundreds of battles and has been scarred, but he has never had the slightest hint of betrayal. I, Xiao Yan, am nineteen years old. During the four years in the northern border, I killed thirteen barbarian generals and defeated twenty-seven enemy formations. I guarded the border without any invaders and protected the people on the border."
"What does collaboration with the enemy mean? What does oversight mean?"
He asked questions, but there was no angry roar, only a deathly cold silence, butIt was more powerful than roaring, and the wind and rain around it seemed to be stagnant for a moment.
